findings.title: New TableWidgetVisualization is wired up with hardcoded empty data
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is on, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of passing the actual `result.data`/`result.meta` and the widget's fields. Because `TableWidgetVisualization` derives its columns from `columns ?? Object.keys(tableData.meta.fields)`, passing an empty `columns` array and empty meta means the table renders zero columns and zero rows regardless of the query results. Any organization that gets this flag enabled will see blank table widgets on all dashboards. If the integration isn't ready, the flag-gated branch should not be merged in this state; otherwise pass the real table data through.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are only filtered out when the user is searching
findings.body: The new `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES = ['is_segment', 'project_id', 'received']` list is only applied inside the search-filter branch: `if (!searchQuery.trim()) { return sorted; }` returns the unfiltered attribute list whenever the search box is empty. The intent of the change is clearly to never display these internal attributes, but in the default (no search) view they are still shown in the span attributes panel. The hidden-attribute exclusion needs to be applied to the base list, not just to the search-filtered list.

findings.title: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values() positionally, which can mismatch error IDs and payloads
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds the result with `zip(error_ids, events.values())` and then filters out entries whose data is None. This assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict whose iteration order exactly matches the input `error_ids` order and that every requested key is present. If nodestore returns events in a different order, or omits missing/expired nodes entirely (which the caching backend can do), every error after the missing one gets paired with the wrong event payload: the summary sent to Seer will attach one error's title/message to another error's ID. Look up each event by its node id (e.g. iterate `zip(node_ids, error_ids)` and index into the dict, or use `events.get(node_id)`) instead of relying on positional alignment.

findings.title: All error events are injected into every paginated segment page
findings.body: `get` paginates over recording segments (`GenericOffsetPaginator` with `on_results=functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, error_events)`), and `analyze_recording_segments` merges the full `error_events` list into the log stream for whichever page of segments is being processed. `get_request_data` resets `error_idx` to 0 on each call, so for replays whose segments span multiple pages, every error line ('User experienced an error...') is emitted on every page, and errors far outside the page's time range are interleaved with that page's breadcrumbs. Clients fetching multiple pages will send duplicated error context to Seer (inflating the LLM prompt with repeats) and get chronologically misleading merges. Errors should be scoped to the page's segment time range (or deduplicated across pages).

findings.title: Flex justify="right" is not a valid justify value
findings.body: The replaced wrapper uses `<Flex justify="right">`. `right` is not part of the justify-content value union the shared `Flex` component accepts (flex-start/flex-end/center/space-between/space-around/space-evenly), so this will either fail type checking or silently produce no justification, leaving the Delete client button left-aligned instead of right-aligned as before. Use `justify="flex-end"`.

findings.title: get_environment_info issues a Snuba query per issue inside PR comment generation
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()`, which performs an eventstore/Snuba lookup, and it is invoked once per issue from the GitHub/GitLab `get_comment_body` list comprehension (up to 5 issues per merged-PR comment). That adds up to 5 sequential Snuba queries inside the PR comment celery task on top of the existing top-issues query, increasing task latency and Snuba load on every merged PR with suspect issues. Consider fetching environments for all issues in one query, or skipping environment info when the additional cost isn't justified.
